card.architecture: HunyuanVideo 1.5 i2v (480p cfg-distilled fp8) + 1080p super-resolution second pass — IMAGE-TO-VIDEO
card.summary: The official two-stage HunyuanVideo 1.5 pipeline: generate at 480p, then a latent upsampler + 1080p SR distilled model refine to full 1080p. Two UNets resident — 24 GB (spills). The source image is the first frame.
card.pick_when: You want 1080p HunyuanVideo 1.5 output and have a 24 GB card.

prompt.guidance: Describe the motion/scene in a sentence. The image is the first frame; output is upscaled to 1080p.
prompt.example: she smiles and turns her head as petals drift past, gentle camera push-in
prompt.overview: Keep the uploaded image as the first frame and write a prompt focused on motion dynamics (how subject and scene move/evolve) plus optional camera movement, not the static appearance.
prompt.instructions: HunyuanVideo 1.5 (Qwen2.5-VL + ByT5 encoders) follows an official I2V formula: 'Subject Motion Dynamics + Scene Motion Dynamics + [Camera Movement]', using concise, direct vocabulary (bracketed layers are optional). Tencent says longer, detailed prompts measurably improve output, and recommends sequencing actions in temporal order with connectives ('first... then... meanwhile... finally...') and concrete actions plus spatial references (left/right frame, foreground/background) instead of abstract emotion words. Wrap any in-frame text in quotation marks (ByT5 glyph encoder renders it). Built-in prompt rewriting auto-expands short prompts, but the formula works directly without an external rewriter.
do: Follow the I2V formula: Subject motion dynamics + Scene motion dynamics + optional Camera movement
Describe how things MOVE and what changes (legs alternating, grass rushing backward), not static appearance
Sequence actions temporally with connectives: 'first... then... meanwhile... finally...'
Use concrete observable actions and spatial references (left/right frame, foreground/background)
Use standard camera-move terms: dolly in/out, pan, tilt, orbit, tracking, crane, follow, fixed/static
Wrap on-screen text in quotation marks to trigger accurate text rendering
Layer optional lighting/style/atmosphere keywords (cinematic lighting, golden hour, photorealism)
dont: Don't re-describe the static first-frame content - focus the prompt on motion
Don't rely on vague emotional language ('beautiful', 'sad mood') without concrete action cues
Don't assume you must run an external rewriter - the formula works directly
Don't lean on negative prompts to fix quality, especially on distilled checkpoints
Don't stuff contradictory camera moves or styles into one clip
examples: The camera follows the puppy as it runs forward on grass, its four legs alternating, tail held high and wagging. Blades of grass are kicked up, ears bounce with rhythm, tongue hangs from open mouth panting gently. Background grass rushes backward; distant sky is pale blue with drifting clouds.

The woman slowly turns her head toward the window, then a faint smile spreads across her face as wind lifts strands of her hair; meanwhile sheer curtains billow inward and soft afternoon light shifts across her cheek. Camera slowly dollies in.
prompt.negative_guidance: Negatives are supported (default empty) and apply only to standard checkpoints at the recommended CFG~6; on the cfg-distilled and step-distilled variants (guidance_scale=1) CFG is effectively off, so negatives have little to no effect. The non-distilled cfg-480/cfg-720 variants run real CFG and do respond to negatives.

edit_use_cases: image-to-video: animate the current picture and upscale to 1080p with HunyuanVideo 1.5

speed.measured_note: Two-stage 480p→1080p; not yet benchmarked on this box.
